hypotheses.title: Symbol resolution is quadratic in consecutive else-less `if` statements (blockSymbolResolver parent-chain walks)
hypotheses.issue: nodebuilder/node_builder.go:generateAndAddBLangStatements wraps all statements following an `if` without `else` in a new BLangBlockStmt, so K such ifs in a row nest K blocks deep (a common guard-clause shape). In semantics/internal/symbols/symbol_resolver.go each nested block gets its own blockSymbolResolver, and several hot operations recurse up the whole parent chain: GetCtx() and GetPkgID() just delegate to parent (called several times per new scope in newScopedBlockResolver/newFunctionResolver and on many per-reference paths); markUsed/markInit delegate to parent until reaching the function-level resolver (the only one with a varTracker); GetSymbol recurses through every level and at each level calls model.(*SymbolSpace).GetSymbol, which takes an RWMutex read lock and does a map lookup even though nearly every one of these wrapper block spaces is empty. Each statement/reference therefore costs O(depth), making stage 3 O(K^2): 1000 ifs/function -> 1.7s, 2000 -> 7.4s, 4000 -> 33s of symbol resolution, while every other frontend stage stays below ~200ms. CPU profile on the reproducer: blockSymbolResolver.GetSymbol 3.7s cum, RWMutex atomic add 1.8s, GetCtx 1.3s, markUsed 1.1s, GetPkgID 0.8s.

reproducer.generator:
import sys
# usage: gen.py out.bal NFUNCS NVARS NIFS
out, nf, nv, ni = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
L = ['import ballerina/io;', '']
for f in range(nf):
    L.append(f'function f{f}(int input) returns int {{')
    for v in range(nv):
        L.append(f'    int v{v} = input + {v};')
    L.append('    int acc = 0;')
    for i in range(ni):
        L.append(f'    if v{i % nv} > {i} {{')
        L.append(f'        acc = acc + v{(i * 7) % nv};')
        L.append('    }')
    L.append('    return acc;')
    L.append('}')
    L.append('')
L.append('public function main() {')
L.append('    int s = 0;')
for f in range(nf):
    L.append(f'    s = s + f{f}(1);')
L.append('    io:println(s);')
L.append('}')
open(out, 'w').write('\n'.join(L) + '\n')
reproducer.command: python3 gen.py repro.bal 8 10 2000 && go build -o /tmp/bal ./cli/cmd && /tmp/bal run --stats repro.bal   # also: ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> repro.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: (1) Cache ctx and pkgID on blockSymbolResolver at construction (newFunctionResolver/newScopedBlockResolver) so GetCtx/GetPkgID are O(1); parent/scope are never reassigned so the cache cannot go stale. (2) Store trackerOwner = nearest ancestor resolver owning a varTracker (computed in O(1) from the parent's own trackerOwner) and have markInit/markUsed jump straight to it when varTracker is nil; keep the existing fallthrough to parent when a tracker exists but the symbol is not tracked. (3) Make blockSymbolResolver.GetSymbol iterative over the chain of block resolvers; captured must be true iff any resolver crossed below the declaring block (including the starting one) has captureRegionClosure, and only for blockScopeKind results; fall back to parent.GetSymbol when reaching a non-block resolver. (4) Add an atomic named-symbol counter to model.SymbolSpace (updated under the write lock in AddSymbol) so GetSymbol on an empty space returns immediately without the RWMutex. Remaining cost (~0.8s) is still O(depth) per lookup (one atomic load per level); removing it entirely would need empty blocks to skip to the nearest non-empty ancestor (careful: symbols can be added to a block after nested resolvers are created) or stop nesting statements after else-less ifs in the node builder (changes AST goldens). make test and make test-race pass.

notes: Also noticed (not pursued): uninitialized-variable analysis in semantics/internal/cfg/uninitialized_var_analyzer.go clones a map of every tracked variable per block (mergePredecessors/analyze/mergeStates), O(blocks x vars); 8 funcs x 1000 vars x 1000 ifs -> CFG Analysis ~2.2s, 2.9GB RSS. A bitset indexed by local would fix it.
